pages.notes: Chapter X opener; the opening chapter essay and the section-opening prose are motivational and not inventoried. Section X.1 begins: eq (1) states Lim/Colim as adjoints of the diagonal (remark1); eq (2) states the initial object as a (co)limit (remark2, which continues onto PDF 241).

remark2 concludes here (proof that e = Lim Id_C). Lemma 1 (limiting cone over Id gives an initial object) and Theorem 2 (formal criterion for existence of a left adjoint) with full proof. NOTE: no 'Theorem 1' appears in X.1 - Mac Lane uses a single shared counter for lemmas/theorems/corollaries per section, so 'Lemma 1, Theorem 2' is items 1 and 2, not a numbering gap.

Section X.1 Exercises 1-5. Section X.2 (Weak Universality) opens: weak-universal-arrow definition (in running prose) and Theorem 1 (a small-complete category has an initial object iff it has a small weakly-initial set); thm1 proof continues onto PDF 243.

X.2 Theorem 1 proof (pullback/pentagon diagram; cites 'Lemma 1.1' = X.1 Lemma 1 under Mac Lane's section.item cross-ref convention) concludes. Section X.3 (The Kan Extension) opens: the precomposition functor A^K (construction1) and the unnumbered bold Definition of a right Kan extension (def1, continues onto PDF 244).

Right-Kan universal property / natural bijection eq (2) concludes def1. remark1: existence of all right Kan extensions along K makes A^K acquire a right adjoint Ran_K. Theorem 1 (right Kan extension as a pointwise limit over the comma category) statement begins; continues onto PDF 245-246.
Continuation of X.3 Theorem 1: full statement (eqs 3-4) and proof (eqs 5-7, functoriality of R and naturality of the counit).

X.3 Theorem 1 proof ends (eq 8, q.e.d.). Corollary 2 (M small, A complete: Ran exists / A^K has right adjoint); Corollary 3 (K full+faithful gives an iso counit) with proof; Corollary 4 (extension along a full-subcategory inclusion) begins and continues onto PDF 247. The 'Kan [1958]' note on cor2 is historical (not inventoried).

cor4 proof ends. Left Kan extension Lan_K defined dually (universal from T to A^K; bijection eq 9; pointwise colimit formula eq 10) = def2. Section X.3 Exercises 1-5. Section X.4 (Kan Extensions as Coends) opens with Theorem 1 (coend formula for Lan); continues onto PDF 248.
X.4 Theorem 1 proof (chain of natural isomorphisms eq 2, via Yoneda + Fubini). Theorem 2 (the unit of the coend left Kan extension, as copower injection composed with the ending-wedge component).

Opens with a 'two formulas' comparison of the coend (X.4.1) and colimit (X.3.10) formulas for Lan - not separately inventoried (both formulas already captured; the agreement follows from uniqueness of Lan). remark1: the dual end formula for Ran (eq 3). construction1: additive/Ab-enriched Kan extensions via the cotensor eq (4). remark2: left derived functors as a right Ab-Kan extension (eq 5); this example begins here and its concluding sentence lands on PDF 250 (context, not owned).

Top of page finishes the additive/derived-functors discussion of X.4 (unit T_* K -> T is the identity; Cartan-Eilenberg pointer) that STARTED on PDF 249 (printed 242, maclane:X.4:remark2) -> already owned by the A range. The five X.4 Exercises begin here (first owned page of the B range). Section X.5 (Pointwise Kan Extensions) opens with the prose 'preservation of a Kan extension' definition and Theorem 1.
Theorem 1 proof continues from p250 (formula (2) Nat(FH,L)=Nat(H,GL) and the bijection chain). Corollary 2, the unnumbered 'pointwise' Definition, and Theorem 3 all start here.

Theorem 3 proof continues from p251. The unnumbered 'missing Lemma', Corollary 4, and the single X.5 Exercise appear here. Section X.6 (Density) opens at the bottom with the informal dense-subcategory definition (maclane:X.6:def1), whose formal Definition block spans onto p253.

Formal 'dense functor' Definition block (maclane:X.6:def1, recorded under its start p252) completes here with formula (1) and canonical cone Q^c. New starts: the '* is dense in Set' example (remark1), the codense Definition, Proposition 1, Proposition 2.

Corollary 3 (Yoneda embedding codense); the unnumbered dual-of-Proposition-2 density criterion (remark2); the proven application that finitely generated abelian groups / the one-object subcategory Z(+)Z are dense in Ab (remark3); then the five X.6 Exercises.
Section X.7 (All Concepts Are Kan Extensions) opens with Theorem 1 (colimit = Lan along K_1) and Theorem 2 (formal criteria for an adjoint). Theorem 2's proof spans onto p256.

Theorem 2 proof continues (converse direction, triangular identities). Proposition 3 (absolute Kan extension Ran_G 1_A = F); the Lan_I/Ran_I = identity remark; and the identity-Kan-extension end computation that recovers Yoneda (remark2), which concludes on p257.

Yoneda-recovery derivation (maclane:X.7:remark2, recorded under its start p256) finishes at the top ('The result is just the Yoneda Lemma'). Three X.7 Exercises (Ex 3 has parts a,b,c on the codensity monad). Chapter closes with an unnumbered historical 'Notes.' block (Benabou/Kan/Ulmer/Lawvere/Cartan-Eilenberg/Isbell/Dubuc/Kelly) - not inventoriable.

items.name: (co)limits as adjoints of the diagonal functor
items.statement_summary: The diagonal functor Delta : C -> C^J has the limit functor Lim as a right adjoint and the colimit functor Colim as a left adjoint whenever all J-indexed limits and colimits exist in C; i.e. Colim -| Delta -| Lim. This is the adjoint characterization of limits/colimits used to set up the rest of the section.

items.name: initial object as a limit of the identity (and colimit of the empty functor)
items.statement_summary: An initial object of a category C is simultaneously the colimit of the empty functor 0 -> C (0 the empty/ordinal-zero category) and the limit of the identity functor Id_C; conversely e = Lim Id_C when that limit exists. Establishes that initial objects are expressible as limits, motivating Lemma 1 and Theorem 2.

items.name: limiting cone over the identity yields an initial object
items.statement_summary: If lambda : d => Id_C is a cone from d to the identity functor and F : J -> C is a functor whose restriction lambda-F : d => F is a limiting cone for F, then d is an initial object of C. (Converse to the fact that an initial object gives a limiting cone over Id_C.)

items.name: Formal criterion for the existence of an adjoint
items.statement_summary: A functor G : A -> X has a left adjoint iff (i) G preserves all limits that exist in A and (ii) for each x in X the comma-category projection Q : (x/G) -> A has a limit in A. When so, a left adjoint is Fx = Lim(Q : (x/G) -> A), and the adjunction transpose of an arrow g : x -> Ga is the limiting-cone component lambda_g : Fx -> Qg = a.

items.name: dual of Theorem 2
items.statement_summary: State the dual of Theorem 2 (the formal criterion for the existence of a right adjoint: a functor has a right adjoint iff it preserves all existing colimits and each relevant comma projection has a colimit).

items.name: Benabou: formal criterion for representability
items.statement_summary: For C with small hom-sets and * the one-point set, prove that K : C -> Set is representable iff (i) K preserves all limits existing in C and (ii) the comma projection Q : (*/K) -> C has a limit r in C; the limiting cone lambda : r => Q then assigns to each h in Kc an arrow lambda_h : r -> c, and h |-> lambda_h is a representation K ~= C(r, -).

items.name: formal criterion for a universal arrow
items.statement_summary: For X with small hom-sets, prove that a universal arrow from x in X to G : A -> X exists iff (i) the functor X(x, G-) : A -> Set preserves all limits and (ii) the comma projection Q : (x/G) -> A has a limit in A.

items.name: refinements of the formal existence criteria
items.statement_summary: (a) In Theorem 2, show hypothesis (i) may be weakened to 'G preserves the particular limits required to exist in (ii)'. (b) In Exercise 2, show hypothesis (i) may be weakened to 'K preserves the limit of Q'.

items.name: Benabou: representables and adjoints via a freely adjoined object
items.statement_summary: For C with small hom-sets and K : C -> Set, form C_K by adjoining one new object infinity with hom-sets C_K(infinity, c) = Kc, C_K(c, infinity) = empty, C_K(infinity, infinity) = * (one-point), with appropriate composition; let J_K : C -> C_K be the inclusion. Prove K is representable iff J_K has a left adjoint.

items.name: weak universal arrow (and weak limits/products/coproducts)
items.statement_summary: Given G : A -> X and x in X, a weak universal arrow from x to G is a pair <r, w : x -> Gr> with r in A such that every f : x -> Ga factors as f = Gf' o w for some, not necessarily unique, f' : r -> a (universal arrow minus uniqueness). Dropping uniqueness in the analogous universals defines weak products, weak limits, and weak coproducts.

items.name: weakly-initial set gives an initial object (second proof of Freyd existence)
items.statement_summary: If D is a small-complete category with small hom-sets, then D has an initial object iff it has a small set S of objects that is weakly initial (for every d in D there is s in S with an arrow s -> d). Proof forms the limit of the inclusion of the full subcategory on S. This is a second proof of Freyd's initial-object existence theorem (V.6.1).

items.name: precomposition (restriction) functor A^K on functor categories
items.statement_summary: For K : M -> C and a category A, the functor A^K : A^C -> A^M sends a functor S : C -> A to the composite SK = S o K and a natural transformation sigma : S => S' to the whiskered sigma-K : SK => S'K. Right and left Kan extensions along K are defined as the right and left adjoints of A^K.

items.name: right Kan extension Ran_K T
items.statement_summary: Given K : M -> C and T : M -> A, a right Kan extension of T along K is a pair <R, epsilon : RK => T> with R in A^C and epsilon universal as an arrow from A^K to T: for every S with alpha : SK => T there is a unique sigma : S => R with alpha = epsilon . (sigma K). Equivalently a natural bijection Nat(S, Ran_K T) ~= Nat(SK, T); R = Ran_K T is unique up to natural iso.

items.name: Ran_K as right adjoint to A^K
items.statement_summary: If every functor T in A^M has a right Kan extension <R, epsilon_T : RK => T> along K, then the assignment T |-> R = Ran_K T is (the object function of) a right adjoint to the precomposition functor A^K, with the universal epsilon as the counit of the adjunction A^K -| Ran_K.

items.name: Right Kan extension as a pointwise limit
items.statement_summary: For K : M -> C and T : M -> A such that for each c in C the composite T o Q over the comma category (c/K) has a limit in A, set Rc = Lim_{(c/K)} T (= Lim_f Tm) with limiting cone lambda; each g : c -> c' induces a unique Rg between the limits commuting with the cones, defining a functor R : C -> A, and the components epsilon_n = lambda_{1_{Kn}} give epsilon : RK => T. Then <R, epsilon> is the right Kan extension of T along K (computed pointwise as a comma-category limit).

items.name: existence of right Kan extensions for M small, A complete
items.statement_summary: If M is small and A is complete, then every functor T : M -> A has a right Kan extension along any K : M -> C, and consequently the precomposition functor A^K : A^C -> A^M has a right adjoint Ran_K. (Kan's original case is A = Set.)

items.name: full-and-faithful K gives an invertible counit
items.statement_summary: If K in Theorem 1 is full and faithful, then the universal arrow (counit) epsilon : RK => T of the right Kan extension R of T along K is a natural isomorphism RK ~= T. Proof: 1_{Kn} is initial in the comma category (Kn/K), so RKn = Lim over (Kn/K) is computed at that initial object, giving epsilon_n = 1.

items.name: Kan extension as an actual extension along a full-subcategory inclusion
items.statement_summary: If M is a full subcategory of C and T : M -> A is a functor such that each composite over (c/K) has a limit in A, then there is a functor R : C -> A with RK = T (R genuinely extends T) for which the identity natural transformation 1 : RK => T makes R the right Kan extension of T along the inclusion K : M -> C. Proof applies Corollary 3 to the insertion.

items.name: left Kan extension Lan_K T
items.statement_summary: Dually, a left Kan extension of T : M -> A along K : M -> C is a pair <L, eta : T => LK> with eta universal as an arrow from T to A^K, giving a natural bijection Nat(Lan_K T, S) ~= Nat(T, SK) in S. When the requisite colimits exist, Lc = Colim over the comma category (K/c) of the composite T o P, with P : (K/c) -> M the projection <m, Km -> c> |-> m. Lan_K is left adjoint to A^K.

items.name: Kan extensions of subsets along a set map
items.statement_summary: With A the arrow category 2 and M, C sets, a functor T : M -> 2 is a subset of M. Show 2^M is the contravariant power set P(M), that Lan_K T is the direct image K[T] of the subset T under the function K, and describe Ran_K T (the coimage/dual construction).

items.name: left Kan extension of a representable functor
items.statement_summary: For A = Set and M, C with small hom-sets, show that the left Kan extension along K of the representable functor M(m, -) is the representable C(Km, -), with unit eta : M(m, -) => C(Km, -) determined by eta(m) = 1_{Km}.

items.name: non-existence of Kan extensions along a non-surjective set map
items.statement_summary: If M, C, A are all sets with A having at least two elements and K : M -> C not surjective, prove that neither Lan_K T nor Ran_K T exists (the missing values in C have no canonical extension).

items.name: Ulmer: weakening Corollary 3's full-and-faithful hypothesis
items.statement_summary: (Ulmer.) Show Corollary 3 (invertible counit) still holds when 'K is full and faithful' is replaced by 'K is full, and as faithful as T', where K is as faithful as T means: for arrows h, h' : m -> n in M, Kh = Kh' implies Th = Th'.

items.name: colimit as a left Kan extension along adjoining a terminal object
items.statement_summary: For any category M let M_infinity be M with a new object infinity adjoined, terminal in M_infinity. For T : M -> A prove from first principles that a colimiting cone for T is exactly a left Kan extension of T along the inclusion M in M_infinity (its value at infinity), and conversely.

items.name: Kan extensions as coends (left Kan extension as a coend of copowers)
items.statement_summary: Given K : M -> C and T : M -> A such that all copowers C(Km', c) . Tm exist in A, then T has a left Kan extension L = Lan_K T along K iff for each c in C the coend integral^m C(Km, c) . Tm exists, in which case (Lan_K T)c = integral^m C(Km, c) . Tm. Proof via Yoneda and Fubini for ends/coends.

items.name: unit of the coend left Kan extension
items.statement_summary: For the coend Kan extension of Theorem 1, the universal arrow (unit) eta : T => LK has component at n in M equal to the composite of the copower coprojection i_{1_{Kn}} : Tn -> C(Kn, Kn) . Tn (for f = 1_{Kn}) followed by the ending-wedge component omega into the coend integral^m C(Km, Kn) . Tm = (Lan_K T)(Kn).

items.name: right Kan extension as an end of powers
items.statement_summary: Dually to Theorem 1, the right Kan extension is given by the end formula (Ran_K T)c = integral_m Tm^{C(c, Km)}, valid whenever the powers a^X (X a set, a in A) and the indicated end exist in A.

items.name: additive (Ab-enriched) Kan extension via cotensor
items.statement_summary: For Ab-categories M, C, A and additive K, T, the additive right Ab-Kan extension is an additive functor R' : C -> A with the Kan bijection natural over additive functors S; it generally differs from the ordinary Ran_K T but is computed by the end formula (3) with the power a^C replaced by the cotensor c^C defined by the natural adjunction A(b, c^C) ~= Ab(C, A(b, c)) (e.g. in A = R-Mod, a^C = Ab(C, a)).

items.name: left derived functors as a right Ab-Kan extension
items.statement_summary: The left derived functors T_n of a right-exact T : R-Mod -> Ab, forming a connected sequence with the universal property (T_0 = T; any connected sequence S_n with S_0 => T_0 extends uniquely to {S_n} -> {T_n}), can be packaged as a single additive functor T_* : E -> Ab on the Ext-graded Ab-category E (objects <C, n>, hom-groups Ext_R^{n-m}(C, B) with Yoneda product). Then Nat(S_* K, T) ~= Nat(S_*, T_*) exhibits T_* as the right Ab-Kan extension of T = T_0 along the embedding K : R-Mod -> E, with identity unit.

items.name: coends give the Lan_K colimits
items.statement_summary: Assuming the coends of Theorem X.4.1 exist, prove they yield exactly the colimits required by the colimit formula (3.10) for Lan_K.

items.name: Lan_K and Ran_K as functors of T
items.statement_summary: For fixed K, describe Lan_K T and Ran_K T, where they exist, as functors of the variable T.

items.name: composition of right Kan extensions (Dubuc)
items.statement_summary: (Dubuc.) Given that Ran_K T exists and L : C -> D is any functor, prove Ran_{LK} T exists iff Ran_L(Ran_K T) exists, and that then the two functors together with their universal arrows are equal.

items.name: Kan extension as a coend in the functor category A^C (Ulmer; Day-Kelly)
items.statement_summary: (Ulmer; Day-Kelly.) If all copowers C(Km',c).Tm exist, show <m',m> |-> C(Km',-).Tm is the object part of a functor M^op x M -> A^C; prove T has a left Kan extension along K iff this bifunctor has a coend, and then Lan_K T = integral^m C(Km,-).Tm; describe the universal arrow for Lan_K T via the coend.

items.name: existence of Ran_K T via the limit formula in A^C (Ulmer)
items.statement_summary: (Ulmer.) Dually to Exercise 4, obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of Ran_K T in terms of the limit/end formula, interpreted in the functor category A^C.

items.name: preservation of a right Kan extension by a functor
items.statement_summary: Given C -K-> M -T-> A -G-> X and a right Kan extension Ran_K T with counit epsilon, G is said to preserve this right Kan extension when the composite G o Ran_K T is a right Kan extension of GT along K with counit G(epsilon) : G(Ran_K T)K -> GT; this condition is strictly stronger than the bare isomorphism G o Ran_K T ~= Ran_K(GT).

items.name: right adjoints preserve right Kan extensions
items.statement_summary: If G : A -> X has a left adjoint F, then G preserves every right Kan extension that exists in A. Proof uses the adjunction bijection A(Fx,a) ~= X(x,Ga) promoted to Nat(FH,L) ~= Nat(H,GL) and the definition of the right Kan extension.

items.name: representables preserve right Kan extensions
items.statement_summary: If R with counit epsilon : RK -> T is a right Kan extension and A has small hom-sets and all small copowers, then for each a in A the functor A(a,R-) : C -> Set is the right Kan extension of A(a,T-) : M -> Set with counit A(a,epsilon-); proved because A(a,-) : A -> Set has the left adjoint X |-> X.a (the copower).

items.name: pointwise right Kan extension
items.statement_summary: Given C -K-> M -T-> A with A having small hom-sets, a right Kan extension R of T along K is pointwise when it is preserved by all representable functors A(a,-) : A -> Set, a in A.

items.name: pointwise Kan extension exists iff comma-category limits exist
items.statement_summary: A functor T : M -> A has a pointwise right Kan extension along K : M -> C iff for every c in C the limit of the composite (c down K) -> M -T-> A exists; when it does, Ran_K T is given by the limit formulas of Theorem X.3.1. Forward: A(a,-) preserves limits so the limit-formula extension is pointwise; converse via the cone/naturality bijection.

items.name: cones over the comma category vs natural transformations
items.statement_summary: For K : M -> C, a in A, c in C there is a bijection between cones from a to the composite T o Q (Q : (c down K) -> M the comma projection, so TQ : (c down K) -> A) and natural transformations C(c,K-) -> A(a,T-): a cone assigns tau(f,m):a->Tm to each f:c->Km with tau(Kh o f,m')=Th o tau(f,m), matching beta with component beta_m f = tau(f,m) under the naturality beta_{m'}(Kh o f)=Th o beta_m f.

items.name: pointwise Kan extension via a hom-set bijection
items.statement_summary: R with counit epsilon : RK -> T is a pointwise right Kan extension of T along K iff for all a in A and c in C the map A(a,Rc) -> Nat(C(c,K-), A(a,T-)) is a bijection, where g:a->Rc is sent to the natural transformation whose m-component takes f in C(c,Km) via C(c,Km) -R-> A(Rc,RKm) -A(g,epsilon_m)-> A(a,Tm).

items.name: canonical comparison map for preservation
items.statement_summary: In the setting C -K-> M -T-> A -G-> X, if Ran_K T and Ran_K GT both exist with counits epsilon, epsilon', prove there is a unique natural transformation (the canonical map) w : G o Ran_K T -> Ran_K GT with epsilon' . wK = G(epsilon), and that G preserves Ran_K T iff w is an isomorphism.

items.name: dense functor / dense subcategory
items.statement_summary: A functor K : M -> C is dense when for each c in C the colimit of (K down c) -P^c-> M -K-> C equals c, with colimiting cone the canonical cone Q^c (Q^c<m,f>=f, viewed as Q^c : K P^c -> c); equivalently the canonical map Colim K P^c -> c is an isomorphism. A subcategory M of C is dense when its inclusion is a dense functor, i.e. every object is a canonical colimit of the objects of M along the arrows m->c.

items.name: the one-point set is dense in Set
items.statement_summary: Example: the one-point set * is dense in Set; for each set X the comma category (* down X) is the discrete category of elements x in X, and density (1) states that X is the coproduct (disjoint union) of X copies of *, i.e. a function out of X is determined by its values.

items.name: codense functor
items.statement_summary: Dually, K : M -> C is codense when for each c in C the limit of (c down K) -Q-> M -K-> C equals c, with limiting cone the canonical cone sending <f:c->Km> to f; this limit is exactly the one appearing in the definition of Ran_K K.

items.name: codense iff identity is the pointwise Ran_K K
items.statement_summary: The functor K : M -> C is codense iff the identity functor Id_C, together with the identity natural transformation id : K -> K, is the pointwise right Kan extension of K along K (i.e. Ran_K K = Id_C, pointwise).

items.name: codense iff the functor c |-> C(c,K-) is full and faithful
items.statement_summary: K : M -> C is codense iff for all a,c in C the map C(a,c) -> Nat(C(c,K-), C(a,K-)), f |-> f* = C(f,K-) ('compose with f on the right'), is a bijection; equivalently iff the functor C^op -> Ens^M given by c |-> C(c,K-):M->Ens is full and faithful (hom-sets of M lying in Ens).

items.name: the Yoneda embedding is codense
items.statement_summary: If the hom-sets of M lie in a full category Ens of sets, then the Yoneda embedding Y : M -> (Ens^M)^op, Ym = M(m,-), is codense; equivalently, every functor M -> Ens is a canonical limit of representable functors. Proved directly from the Yoneda Lemma.

items.name: dense iff c |-> C(K-,c) is full and faithful (dual of Prop 2)
items.statement_summary: Dual of Proposition 2: K : M -> C is dense iff the functor C -> Ens^{M^op} given by c |-> C(K-,c) is full and faithful.

items.name: finitely generated abelian groups are dense in Ab
items.statement_summary: Application (proved): the full subcategory of finitely generated abelian groups is dense in Ab; more strongly the full subcategory on the single object Z(+)Z is dense in Ab. Proof: Ab(A,B) -> Nat(Ab(K-,A),Ab(K-,B)) is a bijection - injective since homomorphisms agreeing on cyclic subgroups agree everywhere, surjective by evaluating a transformation on the maps Z -> A (and Z(+)Z suffices because groups are defined by binary operations).

items.name: one-object subcategory R(+)R dense in R-Mod
items.statement_summary: In R-Mod, show that the full subcategory on the single object R (+) R (direct sum) is dense.

items.name: single object Z is not dense in Ab
items.statement_summary: Show that the full subcategory of Ab on the single object Z is not dense in Ab.

items.name: density descends to the image category KM
items.statement_summary: For K : M -> C let the image category KM be the subcategory of C with objects all Km (m in M) and arrows all Kh (h in M). Prove that if K is dense then KM is a dense subcategory of C.

items.name: generators via faithfulness of c |-> C(K-,c)
items.statement_summary: Prove that the objects of a subcategory M generate C iff the functor C -> Ens^{M^op} given by c |-> C(K-,c) is faithful.

items.name: density as a coend of copowers
items.statement_summary: If all copowers C(Km',c).Km exist in C, prove K : M -> C is dense iff every object c in C is the coend c = integral^m C(Km,c).Km with coend wedge omega^c_m : C(Km,c).Km -> c given on the copower injections i_f by omega^c_m i_f = f : Km -> c.

items.name: colimits are left Kan extensions along M -> 1
items.statement_summary: A functor T : M -> A has a colimit iff it has a left Kan extension along the unique functor K_1 : M -> 1, and then Colim T is the value of Lan_{K_1} T at the unique object of 1. Dually, right Kan extensions along K_1 give limits.

items.name: formal criteria for the existence of an adjoint
items.statement_summary: G : A -> X has a left adjoint iff the right Kan extension Ran_G 1_A : X -> A exists and is preserved by G; when so, F = Ran_G 1_A is a left adjoint of G and the Kan-extension counit epsilon : (Ran_G 1_A)G -> 1_A is the counit epsilon : FG -> 1 of the adjunction. Proved via the bijection Nat(S,HF) ~= Nat(SG,H) both ways using the triangle identities.

items.name: left adjoint yields an absolute right Kan extension
items.statement_summary: If G : A -> X has a left adjoint F with counit epsilon : FG -> 1, then Ran_G 1_A exists, equals F with counit epsilon, and is preserved by every functor whatsoever - an absolute Kan extension.

items.name: Kan extension along the identity is the identity
items.statement_summary: For the identity functor I : C -> C, the universal property gives at once Lan_I T = T and Ran_I T = T for every T : C -> A.

items.name: the Ran_I end formula recovers the Yoneda Lemma
items.statement_summary: For T : C -> Set with C having small hom-sets, evaluating the end (Ran_I) formula gives Tc = (Ran_I T)c = integral_m Tm^{C(c,m)} = integral_m Set(C(c,m),Tm) ~= Nat(C(c,-),T) (using X^Y=Set(Y,X) and IX.5.2); i.e. the identity-Kan-extension end reproduces the Yoneda Lemma.

items.name: adjunction bijection as an adjoint-square special case
items.statement_summary: Show that the bijection (1) (and (5.2) as well) is a special case of the adjoint-square bijection of Exercise IV.7.4, Nat(HG, G'K) ~= Nat(F'H, KG).

items.name: Yoneda Lemma from the Ran_K limit formula
items.statement_summary: Obtain the Yoneda Lemma from the limit (end) formula for Ran_K T, giving an independent proof of Yoneda not used in the proof of section X.3.

items.name: the codensity monad of K
items.statement_summary: (a) If K : M -> C has a right Kan extension R along itself, with phi : Nat(S,R) ~= Nat(SK,K), prove <R,eta,mu> is a monad on C where eta = phi^{-1}(Id_K) and mu = phi^{-1}(epsilon . R epsilon) - the codensity monad of K. (b) K is codense iff eta is an isomorphism. (c) If G : A -> X has left adjoint F with unit eta:1->GF and counit epsilon:FG->Id, its codensity monad exists and equals <GF, eta, G epsilon F>, the monad of the adjunction.
